steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: Birch, linden, fir, pine...

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: Rose, daisy, orchid, tulip...

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: Sunset, dusk, twilight, night...

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Got all that down? Now let's try reading an entire passage.

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: 'The roses in the garden have bloomed, filling the garden with a sweet scent.'

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: 'I look up at the sky, at the sunset in the distance.'

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: 'It is a... a...'

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: What's the matter? Is something wrong?

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: I don't know this word, Miss Meteorite.

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Let me see...

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Ah, sorry, I must've forgotten to mark it yesterday.

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Okay, repeat after me:

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: (Speaks in Sarkaz)

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: (Repeats after Meteorite)

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Very good.

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: What does it mean?

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: It's a word that describes a very specific scene, one that is...

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Keep moving! Why are you standing in the middle of the road?!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Shit, another damned beggar.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: A beggar? Here?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Don't poke your head out. It might get his attention.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Dammit, he's coming this way.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: So what? Just ignore him.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Sir? Ma'am? Anybody need someone to write a letter for them? I'm only asking for a few coins, or some food.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Hey, Salley, you need this beggar to write a letter for you?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: Gimme a break, what's the point if I can't even read?!

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: Haha, even better! He can read for you, too. Two jobs for one beggar.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary B
steps.text: Get lost.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary A
steps.text: You hear that, bum? Scram. We've got no money and no need for any letters. Everyone I know who ain't dead is right here in this group.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Sir! Wait, sir!

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Sir, please, even just a cup of water!

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: *Sigh*... Over here!

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Do you need a letter written, young lady?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Not interested. But you can have this bread. This is a battlefield, and we don't need what you're selling.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: (Stomach growls)

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: I'm not a beggar. I can't just take something for free.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Do you want to learn to read and write yourself? Those soldiers don't understand the value of words, and they're too old and stuck in their ways. But you're young. It'll be useful to you.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I don't have time for that. We have to keep moving.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: I can come with your group, then. If you decide to study with me, I promise I won't leave until you've gotten the hang of it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: I see... Here, you can have your bread back.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Just keep it and eat up, quick. We still have a long way to go. You can teach me on the way.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Ah, alright.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Do you know how to write your name? I can teach you that first.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: We don't have names, only codenames.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: What's your codename then?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Blunt Wedge. One of the previous captains named me.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: It's a nice name.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Yeah right. The captain told me it means 'useless arrow'.

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: Haha. There's a Sarkaz proverb: 'Beware rusty arrows.' Infection is no joke.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Heh... So what were you doing before the war started?

steps.name: Sarkaz Passerby
steps.text: I was a teacher.
Two months later...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I wonder how long this war will go on.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Wraps wounds)

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: How's your injury?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: It's fine. I disinfected it and wrapped it with bandages. It should heal up soon.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: That's good. What a beautiful day... The sunlight's so warm.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I've almost finished that book that you lent me. Got any others?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Only poems and essays.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Never mind then.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Hey, Blunt Wedge, you got that wound wrapped up?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Yeah, it's fine, I applied the dressings.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: The what now? Whatever, come get your share.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10... 14 heads total. Not bad! Could've made more if we didn't let a few get away.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Frowns)

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Your share of the bounty, plus rations. Okay, later.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Wait, that's not enough.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: What're you talking about?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I killed two snipers and an armored grenadier.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Those are 30 and 50 percent more than standard, per our agreement. So that's 12 gold coins short.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Since when did you learn crunch numbers like that?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Hold out hand) 12 gold coins, or we could sort this out with the captain. And I might mention your little cache while we're at it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: What are getting at?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: No need to play dumb. Your side gig is none of my business, as long as you don't try to screw me over.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: ...Take your money and keep your mouth shut.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Shrugs)

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Haha, you're a quick learner. Not quite what I had in mind for applied math, but it does the job.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: It's just that everything you teach is way too easy.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Well, looks like you've learned everything from me you need to. It's time for me to go.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Here.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Half a sack of gold coins? For me?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Lesson fees for two months.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Well, I'm not going to say no.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Where are you going to go after this?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I heard things are calmer in the east. Maybe there are still a few schools remaining there.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: You know how to use a weapon. You could've made a living as a mercenary. Why insist on making it hard on yourself?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Kazdel won't miss a single sellsword.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Tch... you intellectual types.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: So when will you finish the book? Remember to return it before I leave.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Tomorrow. I'm almost at the end.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: 'Mathilda found the moonlight shining through the windows too bright. She rubbed her eyes and closed the curtains, before falling into slumber in the... er...'

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: What does this word mean? I've never seen it before... let's keep going.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: 'Sitting by the campfire with her friends, Mathilda poked at the chestnuts in the fire. The sweet scent in the... er... was a gift.'

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: That word again? Gah.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: 'Mathilda closed the door, picked up her suitcase, and prepared to get in the car. She thought back to the countless... er... that she spent here...'

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Countless what?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: 'Farewell, those... er...'

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Who are you saying goodbye to, Mathilda?!

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: 'Perhaps in the days to come, she will see more... er..., but there will be no... er... as unforgettable as the... er... here.'

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: How many freaking times does it need to appear in one sentence?!

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: What the heck does it even mean?!

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: That took longer than expected. How was it? You could keep it as little farewell gift, if you like.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Nah, I prefer adventure novels to reading about some girl sitting on a farm. Honestly, it was pretty frustrating to read.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Was there a problem?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Yeah, there was a word in there I'd never seen. I tried to skip it, but it kept showing up, way too often.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Let me see... ah.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: It means a pleasant and serene night.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: ...A what?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Well, a night that's happy.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: That doesn't make any sense. Nights aren't happy or serene.

spans.text: That doesn't make any sense. Nights aren't happy

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Because they're long, dark, and cold. They're dangerous and you have to always stay on guard... I hate the night.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I've spent so many nights thinking I would die right there and become food for nocturnal scavengers, never to see the sunrise again.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: You could understand 'nocturnal scavengers', but not 'a pleasant and serene night'?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I mean, I've seen plenty of animals tearing at dead bodies. I could picture it as soon as you explained it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Well, in that case, let's try picturing it together. Close your eyes.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Gotcha.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Think back to when you were a little girl, sitting by your mother's side one night...

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Stop right there. I've never met my mother.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Well... did you have any other parental figure as you grew up?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: The previous captain found me on the battlefield and raised me.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Well, picture sitting by her side then. How do you feel?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I'm sitting next to her, and she...

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: She pushes me away, tells me the warband has no use for a weak child, and makes me run ten laps around the camp holding a bucket of water in each hand, without spilling a drop.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: My shoulders are starting to get sore.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: A-Alright, let's try something else. You and your friends are sitting by a campfire in the forest. There's a delicious-smelling pot of soup on the fire.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: What do you feel?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I stick my nose out to get a whiff of it...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Exactly!

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Then I turn around and see a hand reaching for my pack, trying to steal my money pouch. Why the heck did the captain even let that known thief in?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: So I feel really pissed and kinda wish he was right here so I could punch him.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: ...Never mind, let's start over.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Alright... it's nighttime. Gentle moonlight sweeps across the land. You wrap your blanket around you and feel your eyelids dropping, dragging you into slumber.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: What do you feel?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Fear.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Artillery fire might rain down on the camp at any moment... I hide under the bed, covering my ears with my friends.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: *Sigh*... Look at what war has done to you children.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Sorry for not getting it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: It's okay. Let me think of another way.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: It's just a word. You don't need to go that far to teach me.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Every year, many new things appear in our lives, and new words are created to describe them.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Most of these words are forgotten as the things they describe disappear, never to be uttered again.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: But some words are special. They're passed down from one person to another, living on in our collective memory.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: That's because they describe something eternal and unchanging. They represent the most precious, foundational spirit of their people.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: They're worth understanding and remembering.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: So... what if I just can't understand it?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Patience, young lady. Give it time to take root.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Look out for the dried branches under your feet. They're overgrown with moss and very slippery after a rain.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Alright. You're talking too much.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Now can you tell me why you woke me up in the middle of the goddamn night?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: You really are grumpy in the morning.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Pardon me, sir, would you care to enlighten me as to why you've brought me to this place?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: (Puts a piece of cloth on the ground)

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Sit.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Sits down on the cloth, confused)

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Here you go.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: ...Canned peaches?!

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I knew you'd like them. I saw the way you were staring when your captain had a can a few days ago.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Hmph, they're not that special. ...So how'd you get your hands on 'em?

spans.text: special. ...So how'd you get your hands on 'em?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I traded a book for two cans, with your captain.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Whoa, that's one valuable book. What was it?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Just an old manuscript. It wasn't doing anyone any good.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Give me a break, I know how the captain has been collecting old books and selling them to the Columbians.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I'm just stating the facts.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: ...There's still half a can left. Want it?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: All yours.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Thanks...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: What do you feel when you look around you?
*Slap*

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Looks at her palm in disgust)

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Too many bugs.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: There's no need to kill them, they don't bite... but never mind that.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I spent a few nights looking for them. I brought you here because they're special.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I can see their backsides glowing.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Huh... I've seen these by the water before, but I didn't know they were bugs. I thought...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Thought what?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I thought they were the ghosts of people killed in battle.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: People do associate them with will-o-wisps found near graves, but they glow in different ways.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Will-o-wisps are caused by gases released by decomposing bodies, which have a very low flash point and ignite when they come into contact with air.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: What about these bugs, then?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: They secrete chemicals that glow, using their respiration to control the biochemical reaction in order to adjust the brightness.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Their abdomens contain a large amount of light-emitting chemicals and cells.
A bug lands on the man's palm, its backside glowing with a blue light.
Soon, more of the insects draw near, until his entire hand is surrounded in light.
The man seems able to speak endlessly about them, using many complicated words that Blunt Wedge does not understand.
She does not feel troubled, however. In fact, what she's feeling is unfamiliar to her.
It's like a little bug is flapping its wings in her heart, slowly ascending, with a light on its butt that is weak and dim, but filled with vitality.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I think I feel something.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: They like to lay their eggs by the water... Wait, what do you feel? Tell me!

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I feel...
The sound of an explosion interrupts her.
The bugs scatter at the noise, their lights disappearing into the dark woods.
A plume of smoke can be seen in the distance, covering the few stars visible in the night sky.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Oh shit! It's coming from the camp!

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Wait, Blunt Wedge! You haven't told me how you felt yet.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: There's no time for that. We need to get back.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: It's important to me. Please, I must know.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Say something, please.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Nothing.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I felt nothing.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I'm sorry, they flew away too fast. I couldn't catch them.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: No, you felt something! I could see it on your face!

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Shakes head frantically)

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Why were you crying if you didn't feel anything?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: (Wipes away the tears roughly)

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Maybe there was nowhere in my heart for it to take root.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Where were you, Blunt Wedge? The captain was asking about you.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I went into the forest.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: In the middle of the night? Why?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: She went on patrol because she was concerned about the enemies that got away a few days ago.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Y-Yeah, I thought they might retaliate.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Well, you were right. They attacked the camp. The night watch was asleep on duty and got his throat slit.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Wasn't Salley on duty?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Yup, he's dead.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: We lost a bunch of supplies in the fire, too. Can't believe we're going hungry after months of hard work... dammit.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Anyone injured?

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: A few guys got burned. But we lost a lot of medical supplies too, so here's hoping they make it.

steps.name: Sarkaz Mercenary
steps.text: Alright, I gotta go. You should find the captain before he gets mad.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Okay...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: You really should go, Blunt Wedge.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Are you... okay?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: You're the one who just had something bad happen to you. Why are you asking me?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: You look so sad...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Don't worry, it's not because of you.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Why, then?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Because of the scorched earth, where nothing will grow again.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: It's getting late. I should go.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: There's no need to see me off. I'll be fine on my own.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Just a little further. We might not see each other again.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I wanted to thank you... You taught me so many useful things. As for that word...

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: I couldn't understand it, but maybe someone else would.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: It's okay. No need to bring it up.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Don't apologize. It's not your fault. Never was.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I've seen many children like you, who've lost their homes, are used to seeing blood and killing, and drift from one battlefield to the next.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: You were the only one who stopped to peruse the knowledge I was peddling.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: For so many years, I believed that knowledge and culture could bring about change, overcome war and violence.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: But in the end, it looks like war has won. It's made a mockery of everything I knew.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Are you giving up? If you won't teach people the true meaning of those words, who else can?

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Won't they disappear from our lives with no one to understand and preserve them?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: All it means is that the beauty those words represented was fleeting. Only pain and suffering remains.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I'm powerless to fight it.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: It's all good. Don't cry.

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Take this book. I've travelled across Kazdel compiling the vocabulary of the land, trying to complete it.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: A dictionary of the Sarkaz language?

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: I haven't written that word down yet. Do it for me, if you ever find help understanding it in the future.

steps.name: Blunt Wedge
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Sarkaz Teacher
steps.text: Wipe away your tears. This is goodbye.

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: ...teorite? Miss Meteorite?

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Oh!

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Ah, yes, it means a night that is pleasant and serene.

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: Oh, I get it now! Thank you!

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: (Pats the child on the head)

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Sarkaz Child
steps.text: Why are you crying?

steps.name: Meteorite
steps.text: Because you're a very smart kid.
